sections.heading: Fully Adhered vs. Mechanically Attached vs. Ballasted EPDM Roofing Systems

c.v: Attachment follows structural needs, wind exposure, and budget.

runs.v: Fully adhered EPDM costs the most but resists wind flutter and suits complex roofs; mechanically attached EPDM installs faster over a deck that holds fasteners; ballasted EPDM costs least but needs a structure rated for the stone and moderate wind exposure. Commercial EPDM thickness is commonly cited at 30 to 100 mils, with 45 and 60 mils most common, in black or white: white EPDM cuts heat absorption and aids energy efficiency on low slope commercial roofs.

sections.heading: What Are the Downsides of EPDM Roofing?

c.v: Common problems are seam failures, shrinkage at flashings, punctures, ponding, surface cracks with age, and heat on a black membrane.

runs.v: The advantages usually win: good UV and ozone resistance, weather resistance in northern climates, and elasticity for seasonal temperature swings, so EPDM suits Newark's extreme weather. Properly installed, it needs minimal maintenance compared with older systems, balances cost-effectiveness with longevity for long-term performance, and is often described as 100% recyclable. Fire ratings depend on the assembly; ballasted and fire-retardant systems can reach Class A.

faqs.q: How long does a commercial EPDM roof last?

runs.v: 15 to 25 years, per InterNACHI, and 25 to 30 in a study attributed via Progressive Materials; EPDM roofing systems can last 20 to 30 years with maintenance, and some industry sources cite 25 to 40.

faqs.q: Why should you choose EPDM over TPO for a commercial roof?

runs.v: EPDM outlasts TPO's 7-to-20-year range and stays elastic in cold; white TPO offers better energy efficiency.

faqs.q: How much does commercial EPDM roofing cost per square foot in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: $7.00 to $10.00 per square foot installed in New Jersey; Newark Quality Roofing provides a free written estimate.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial EPDM roof in Newark, NJ?

runs.v: Yes: on a commercial building, the maintenance exemption covers repairs to only 25% of the roof area in 12 months.

faqs.q: When should a commercial EPDM roof be replaced instead of repaired?

runs.v: When damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof, leaks recur in one spot, or the membrane reaches 15 to 25 years.

faqs.q: How does EPDM handle the Essex County winter?

runs.v: EPDM is flexible and withstands freeze-thaw cycles through an average January low near 25.5°F, per NOAA, so stress lands on seams, not the field.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule for EPDM roof repair and EPDM roof replacement?

runs.v: Repairing more than 25% of a commercial roof in 12 months needs a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Visual inspections, twice a year and after heavy rain, help identify leaks, and common EPDM roof repair work is seam repairs and puncture patches; an EPDM roof replacement removes the existing membrane in a tear off and installs the new roof after preparing the roof substrate.

faqs.q: Who sells EPDM rubber roofing in New Jersey?

runs.v: Manufacturers sell EPDM rubber roofing systems through roofing supply distributors, mostly to contractors, since system warranties generally require an approved installer.
